ARNADO Mayor Kauswagan, Lanao del Norte Dear Mayor Arnado: -BiVÅHENd s. 2015 This has reference to your letter dated 20 ovember 2014 requesting clarification whether Municipal Ordinance No. 006-2014 is p esumed consistent with law and valid based on DILG Opinion No. 16, series of 2009, in relation to Article 110 (d) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic ct No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 and Section 56 of the same Code. We so received your follow-up letter dated 29 April 2015. Based on your representations* Municipal O dinance No. 006-2014 was received by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Lanao del Norte through the Vice-Governor on 02 June 2014. However, more than thirty (30) days after 0 June 2014 had already elapsed but the Sangguniang Panlalawigan has neither appro ed nor disapproved said Municipal Ordinance. According to you, your Municipal De elopment Fund Office (MDFO) loan for purchase Of heavy equipment direty needed by your municipality is delayed as such municipal ordinance is required to 'be submitted t the Central Bank in the processing of said loan. Hence, your subject letter-request. Section 56 of the Local Government Code f 1991 provides and we quote: "Section 56. Revléw of Componen City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Pamala ban. (a) Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the sanggunian panlungsod or»sanggunian bayan shall forward to the sangguniangpanlalavvigan for review, copi s of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local developm nt plans and public investment programs formulated by the local develop ent councils. (b) Within thirty (30) days aft the receipt of copies of such ordinances and resolutions, 'the sangguni panlalawigan shall examine the documents or transmit them to the provin ial attorney, or if there be none, to the provincial prosecutor for prom t examination. The provincial attorney or provincial prosecutor shall, wi •n aperiod often (IO) days from

receipt of the documents, inform the san niang panlalawigan in vvriting of' his comments or recommendations, w •ch may be considered by the sangguniang panlalavvigan in making its de ision. (c) If the Sangguniang panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred u n the sangguniangpanlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned, it sh 11 declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The sangguniang panlalawigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall clvise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has ta en. (d) If no action has been taken b the san ian n]alawi an within thi 30 da after submission of uch an ordinance or resolution the same shall be resumed consistent •th law and therefore valid. ' (Emphasis Supplied) The Department has been consistent with s opinion that the phrase "take action" in Section 56 (d) should mean that the Sanggunia g Panlalawigan, within thirty (30) days upon receipt of the copy of the ordinance, should have issued its legislative action in the form of' a Resolution containing their disapprova in whole or in part any ordinance or resolution submitted to thgm for review. It is not enough that they deliberated, debated and voted on the measure ought to be reviewed ecause what is required of them is the enactment of a legislative document to formally a d finally put to rest a given measure or issue. This document so enacted is imbued with p blic interest, so much so that it shall be the basis of the general public to rely upon in pe forming their respective obligations or asserting their rights in a given territory. Absent t s document, all local legislative debates are left as silent records, thus, unenforceable as ag insc third persons. Thus, after the lapse of such 30-day period, and no Resolution which shall contain the findings of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan on eview of the municipal ordinance was issued by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, it can e validly stated that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan failed to act within 30 days and the o dinance under review can be presumed consistent with law and therefore vaticl. It is settled that when a power is given, and that the power is to be exercised within a prescriptive period, then such prescriptive period s considered a limitation to such power. This is consistent with the principle that "where a tatuteprescribes a time within which a public officer is to perform official acts affecting th rights of others, it is directory as to the time, unless from the nature Of the act, the de nation of time must be considered a limitation on the power of the officer. "1 50 AM Jur, 23, p. 46, cited by Alcantara, Samson, Statutes, 1990 E
